key_insight: AdsNet predicts adsorption energies directly from local atomic environments, combining geometric sensitivity with computation that does not scale with the full surface size.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate computational catalyst screening and local interface relaxation while providing atom-level energy contributions for interpretation.
method: Builds a cutoff-based graph of adsorbate atoms and nearby surface atoms.
Uses equivariant message passing with scalar and vector features to predict adsorption energy in one forward pass.
Derives forces by automatic differentiation for projected-gradient relaxation with adaptive line search.
evidence_signal: Trained on 33,920 DFT structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates, AdsNet reports energy RMSE of 0.032 eV and force RMSE of 0.047 eV/Å.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the reported metals and adsorbates, and sensitivity to interactions outside the local cutoff, require further validation.
paper_title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
